> File a new bug. Is it? It only happens after a line break. The following, for example, works OK: .push{margin: 5px -160px 1.5em 160px} That I don't need to escape. It also works if I apply a hack to my minifier, to put a space after the line break, like this: 
.push{margin:5px
 -160px 1.5em 160px}

CSS is a free-form language  (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-form_language) in which the positioning of characters on the page in program text is not significant. Which characters are used \n \t <space> etc and their number should do not matter. 

This is not currently true for less.js and it makes not fully compatible with CSS syntax. In my humble opinion this should be changed.

As I wrote in a comment above, less.js' parser does not have a tokenizer. There are a lot of comparisons with a normal space (' ') in the code that create peculiar behaviors like the one you described. Something like this should be used: http://www.cdiggins.com/tokenizer.html 

In the past when I had to implement one, I used interfaces similar to Tokenizer.getCurrentToken(), Tokenizer.followingToken(), Tokenizer.previousToken(), Tokenizer.next()
